source_review.notes: Checked current Linux man-pages and kernel documentation for namespace types, user-ID mappings, PID hierarchy, mount propagation, network and cgroup views, time offsets, unshare and setns. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; syscall contracts, kernel behavior, abstract models, deployment guidance and assurance claims remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked process, namespace-vector, user, PID, mount, network, IPC, UTS, cgroup, time, mapping-range and capability notation.
Reviewed independent namespace coordinates, piecewise ID translation, PID ancestry and user-namespace-relative authorization abstraction.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates namespace membership, translated identity, hierarchical visibility and scoped authority.

evidence: Executed seven translations through two disjoint inside-to-outside UID ranges.
Confirmed boundary IDs 0, 999, 2000 and 2099 map correctly while 1000, 1999 and 2100 remain unmapped; independently recomputed the exercise's five mappings.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates range arithmetic only; it implements no Linux map-file authorization, GID setgroups rule, credential or capability behavior.

evidence: Re-derived mapping within a half-open interval as outside start plus inside displacement.
Checked vector coordinate sharing, one-way PID ancestor visibility and capability checks relative to a resource's owning user namespace plus policy.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations are namespace reasoning tools and do not claim a complete formalization of Linux credentials, procfs, capability checks, security hooks or resource authorization.

evidence: Reviewed unmapped IDs, map gaps, setgroups ordering, user-namespace ownership, PID init exit, future-child setns behavior and procfs mismatch.
Reviewed mount propagation, leaked descriptors, persistent namespace handles, physical devices, non-namespaced sysctls, fork exhaustion and mixed namespace vectors.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Identity, privilege, PID, mount, network, persistence, resource, lifecycle and kernel-global boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced clone, unshare and setns effects across user, PID, mount, network, IPC, UTS, cgroup and time namespaces.
Verified scoped capability ownership, nonoverlapping maps, PID ancestry, propagation direction, handle lifetime, layered controls and ordered teardown.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats a container as an orchestrated namespace vector plus credentials, policies, resources and persistent references rather than one kernel object.

evidence: Reviewed isolation coordinate by coordinate, then overlaid bypass handles, credentials, LSM, seccomp, cgroups, rlimits and lifecycle.
Constructed counterexamples for namespace-as-container, inner-root-as-host-root, mount-namespace-as-file-copy, cgroup-namespace-as-limit and namespace-list-as-containment.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable namespace obligations, not a formal proof of Linux, a runtime, container, sandbox, workload or threat model.

evidence: Audited uses of isolated, shared, owned, mapped, visible, joined, persistent, privileged, limited and contained.
Confirmed syscall guarantees, namespace-specific scope, operational composition, examples and assurance limits remain separately labeled.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: A namespaced view is not labeled resource control, inside UID 0 is not labeled host root, a cgroup namespace is not labeled a cgroup limit and hostname is not labeled an authenticated identity.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-086/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, toolchain and environment for UID mapping.
Reviewed required kernel, man-pages, runtime, helper, LSM, seccomp, cgroup, mapping, capability, propagation, descriptor and namespace-object evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes seven arithmetic results only; it provides no evidence for kernel namespace creation, authorization, isolation, resource governance, teardown or security.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed namespaces as independent per-process lookup contexts whose isolation claims require explicit membership vectors, ownership, credentials, resources and persistent handles.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable concerns including clone/unshare/setns, user maps, PID init, procfs, mount propagation, open descriptors, network links, cgroup and time views, layered policy, lifecycle and negative tests. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from namespace vectors and APIs through user ownership, PID hierarchy, mount and network behavior, narrower namespace types, layered controls and lifecycle, followed by twelve obligations, sixteen trade-offs, twenty-five misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, Linux namespace or container-runtime maintainer, security reviewer, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
